newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares trade higher, buoyed by Chidamabaram.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares trade higher, buoyed by Chidamabaram.

text.p: An early rally in Bombay exchanges sparked by the return of former finance minister P. Chidambaram in the government tapered off on Wednesday, but traders expected share prices to consolidate gains.
The market was likely to hold onto current levels, as focus now shifted to the safe passage of the pro-market 1997/98 (April-March) budget, players said.
"The market looks good. A lot of consolidation should take place at these levels," said Nand Kishore Gupta, chief executive officer at Ind-Sec Share & Stock Brokers.
The BSE top 30 index was up 46.01 points, or 1.21 percent at 3,854.66, off a high of 3,879.21
Technical problems at the Bombay exchange on Wednesday led to a delayed opening, traders said.
The National Stock Exchange Index was 19 points higher, or 1.8 pct, at 1076.45, off a high 1088.15.

"It's a good move and should boost investor confidence," said Aditya Rattan, chief representative at Daiwa Securities, referring to the Tamil Maanila Congress (TMC) party's decision late on Tuesday to rejoin the government.

Chidambaram -- a member of the regional party which opted to stay out of the new government earlier this month after TMC leader G.K. Moopanar was passed over in the choice for Prime Minister -- is due to be sworn in as finance minister.

Parliament on Wednesday opened a two-and-a-half week session to debate the budget which slashed personal and corporate taxes, upped foreign portfolio limits in stocks of local companies and proposed allowing firms to buyback their shares.
The budget will be put to vote in the lower house of parliament after the debate.
"The mood is better. Now, with the government in place, a lot of projects should be cleared," said K. R. Choksey, a top member-broker of the BSE.
Local markets did not take a cue from a 179-point overnight surge in the Dow, as attention remained focussed on domestic political factors, traders said.
"Normally, we have noticed a negative correlation with US markets," said the head of dealing at a foreign brokerage. "But, right now, local factors are overshadowing the Dow rise."
Shares of Housing Development and Finance Corporation (HDFC) were quoted 53.75 rupees, or 1.70 percent, higher at 3,226.0 below the day's high of 3,280.0.
The company said its net profit for the year ending March 31 1997 rose 27 percent to 2.48 billion rupees from 1.96 billion in the year-ago period.
